/-!
# Erdős Problem 1094

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1094](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1094)
-/

namespace Erdos1094

open scoped Nat

/--
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1094 :
    {(n, k) : ℕ × ℕ | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1094

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number division in max (n / k) k, whereas the source uses the ordinary quotient n/k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural p and k > 0, p ≤ max (n / k) k is equivalent to p ≤ n / k ∨ p ≤ k, hence to p*k ≤ n ∨ p ≤ k. This is exactly (p : ℝ) ≤ max ((n : ℝ) / k) (k : ℝ). Negating gives identical exceptional pairs for the two formulations, so their finiteness assertions are equivalent. Both the bound equivalence and the equivalence of the complete finite-exception statements were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the webpage's general finiteness conjecture. ELS88 §2 confirms the domain and bound, and additionally proposes a sharper fourteen-exception refinement, which this declaration does not claim. Lean checks proved that 0 < k and 2*k ≤ n imply 1 < n.choose k, so minFac has its genuine least-prime-factor meaning and neither default values nor division by zero are reachable. Further checks covered k = 1, n = 2*k, and equivalence to a bound holding uniformly for all sufficiently large n. Computation over all admissible pairs with n < 80 found genuine exceptions, including (7,3), confirming nonvacuity. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings, and the proved checks have no sorryAx dependency. The source's OPEN status agrees with the file.
